title: Default-path stdin read is unwrapped, so an unreadable stdin reports OPUM_WORKFLOW_LORE_INCOMPATIBLE where --request - reports BINDING_ABSENT
description:
Filed by the LCLI-679 round-1 review and ruled out of that task scope (leader ruling, 2026-10-06: NARROW the docs to the empty-or-absent case; make NO behaviour change to agent.ts:230 inside LCLI-679). UNBLOCKED AND NEXT, after LCLI-679 lands: DEC-165 (opum-doc origin/dev 14b1da7, opum-ai/opum-doc#751) answered the marker-classification question, so the dependency this record used to carry is GONE.

MEASUREMENT. Default path with an unreadable stdin reports OPUM_WORKFLOW_LORE_INCOMPATIBLE, exit 1, where the --request - path reports OPUM_WORKFLOW_LORE_BINDING_ABSENT for the same condition. So the same caller-visible condition is classified two ways depending on which flag path is taken. CORRECTION from the LCLI-679 round-2 review (head afaed00a): a shell-closed fd is normalized by bun to an empty read and yields BINDING_ABSENT, so the EBADF trigger is not reliably reachable; the reliable triggers are EISDIR (stdin bound to a directory) and a programmatic close-then-read.

CAUSE. src/commands/agent.ts:230 calls readFileSync(0, utf8) UNWRAPPED when neither --request nor --request-file is set; the throw falls through emitBindingFailure generic branch (agent.ts:329) to INCOMPATIBLE. Only resolveBindingFile (agent.ts:311) wraps the read and attributes BINDING_ABSENT.

REMEDY, RULED by DEC-165 (3), so this task needs no second round: an unreadable stdin reports OPUM_WORKFLOW_LORE_BINDING_ABSENT on BOTH paths, because from the adapter side no binding was supplied. Wrap the default-path read at agent.ts:230 the way resolveBindingFile does. That changes which marker a caller sees, which is why it is a task of its own rather than part of LCLI-679.

WHILE THERE, also from the round-2 review: src/commands/agent.ts:159 is a bare-path comment still saying contract mode fails closed with OPUM_WORKFLOW_LORE_ABSENT alone, incomplete now that contract mode also emits BINDING_ABSENT. Fix it here; no acceptance criterion covers it.
plan: Extract the wrapped stdin read in src/commands/agent.ts into one helper used by BOTH the default path (agent.ts:230) and resolveBindingFile, so an unreadable stdin reports OPUM_WORKFLOW_LORE_BINDING_ABSENT on each.
Correct the stale agent.ts:158-159 comment so contract mode names both markers (ABSENT and BINDING_ABSENT).
Add a regression test binding stdin to an unreadable fd; assert BINDING_ABSENT on the default path and --request - (pre-fix control: default path emits INCOMPATIBLE).
Validate: bun test (changed file then full suite) and bun run lore check both exit 0.
Commit, push, open PR into dev, and close LCLI-685 in the delivering PR.
implementationNotes: REMEDY RULED, no second round needed (DEC-165 (3), opum-doc origin/dev 14b1da7, opum-ai/opum-doc#751): an UNREADABLE stdin reports OPUM_WORKFLOW_LORE_BINDING_ABSENT on BOTH the default path and --request -, because from the adapter side no binding was supplied. Today the default path reports OPUM_WORKFLOW_LORE_INCOMPATIBLE with exit 1. So the remedy is (a): wrap the default-path read at src/commands/agent.ts:230 the way resolveBindingFile (:311) does, NOT (b) documenting the split. The dependency on the opum-doc section 7.1 question is REMOVED: DEC-165 (4) answered it — the OPUM_WORKFLOW_* markers are governed by opum-doc control-plane spec stable-redacted-errors list, not by lore-cli ADR-0005 error_type rule. This task starts next, after LCLI-679 lands, ahead of LCLI-681, 682 and 683.

Description corrected at the LCLI-679 round-2 review findings: it no longer says UNSTARTED-until-opum-doc (the dependency is removed), the trigger is EISDIR rather than the unreachable EBADF, and the stale agent.ts:159 comment is folded in as WHILE THERE.

CHANGE (src/commands/agent.ts): extracted readBindingFromStdin() — the wrapped readFileSync(0) that attributes an unreadable stdin to OPUM_WORKFLOW_LORE_BINDING_ABSENT — and routed BOTH the default path in runWorkflowBinding (was the bare readFileSync(0, "utf8") at line 231) and the stdin branch of resolveBindingFile through it. TEST (test/lcli685-unreadable-stdin-marker.test.ts): binds fd 0 to a write-only descriptor (read raises EBADF — the portable spelling of the EISDIR field trigger; openSync on a directory is not portable to Windows CI, and a shell-closed fd is normalized by bun to an empty read). Four cases. GREEN post-fix. PRE-FIX CONTROL (stashed only src/commands/agent.ts, kept the test): exactly 2 of 4 red — the DEFAULT-path case and the both-paths-agree case, both because the default path emitted INCOMPATIBLE — while the --request - case and the readable-stdin positive control stayed green.
